newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fedex step up U.S-China link to four a week.
newsitem.headline: Fedex step up U.S-China link to four a week.

text.p: Federal Express is to double its dedicated freighter service from the U.S. to China to four times weekly from April 7 because of unprecedented demand, the airline's senior vice president Asia Pacific division Michael Ducker has told Reuters.
The Anchorage, Beijing, Shanghai, Subic Bay return service, which began last March, is enjoying the highest load factors on the carrier's international network, Ducker said.

"Load factors are 90 plus percent. It is a tremendous market place for us and the doubling of flights within a year of start-up speaks for itself," Ducker said in an interview at his Hong Kong headquarters. DC10-30 freighters will be used for the expanded service possibly switching to newer McDonnell Douglas MD-11 aircraft at a later date.

Growth rates for Fedex business in China was "triple digit" with enormous future potential as Chinese industry evolves to demand services Fedex offers, he said. Lower end manufacturers continue to switch production from other Asian countries to take advantage of China's lower labour costs adding more business. Duckers said the China market is changing substantially from non time definite customers to shippers demanding more frequencies and total logistics service.
The bulk of Fedex business continues to come from multi-nationals with factories in China but mainland companies "are catching on fast."

"Chinese manufacturers and businesses are really starting to compete on a world scale who need and demnnd the huge world- wide network that Fedex offers so you can move something from anywhere to anywhere, he added.
Fedex also plans to expand its service centre network within China by 20 cities a year over the next five years.

Ducker said there are no immediate plans to fly to more Chinese cities. Fedex has traffic rights to fly into Guangzhou but while business there is "very active," Hong Kong continues to be the dominant outlet for the Pearl River region. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
